rv.q: What lifts this adaptation of 1984 above previous attempts to stage it is the combination of faithful storytelling and free-flying theatricality.
Despite being highly stylized, and some might say overproduced, this production's elements all come together to create an utterly disturbing and authentic stage retelling.
It’s well worth catching whether you’re a fan of the book or new to it.

cn.t: Icke and Macmillan's adaptation breathes fresh life into Orwell's dystopian classic through inventive time shifts and narrative techniques, though the complex structure occasionally threatens coherence. Critics praise it as a gripping modern masterpiece.
